title: At McDonald's, AI Decides Price Of Your Big Mac, Discounted Coffee
rephrased_article: **McDonald's** is using AI to set menu prices in the US and some global markets, aiming to boost profits but risking customer alienation and antitrust scrutiny. The system uses machine learning to estimate local willingness to pay, leading to varied pricing for the same items across locations. Franchisees report pressure to use these tools despite concerns over compliance and potential legal risks.

title: Student protests rock France with over 400 detained: Why are schools protesting - explained
rephrased_article: On Tuesday, **France** saw nationwide strikes and student protests against budget cuts and poor education conditions. Civil servants walked off jobs, while students blocked over 400 schools out of 3,700, demanding more teachers and better facilities. At least 10 teachers, several students, and 48 police were injured; 440 people were detained. The protests come two days before Prime Minister **Sébastien Lecornu** presents the draft 2027 budget with €54 billion in cuts.

title: Mihrab conference calls for inclusive approach in mahals
rephrased_article: On Tuesday (September 29), the **Kerala Muslim Jamaat** organized a Mihrab conference in Kerala, calling for mahals to be inclusive and supportive of all community members. **Ponmala Abdul Khader Musliar**, secretary of **Samastha Kerala Jamiyyathul Ulama (Kanthapuram)**, inaugurated the event ahead of Samastha centenary celebrations. Islamic scholar Maliyekkal Sulaiman Saquafi emphasized mahals' role in welfare and progress through education, employment, health, and financial discipline. Rahmathulla Saquafi Elamaram stressed engagement with all age groups through empathy and dialogue. About 500 religious leaders attended the conference.

title: Madras High Court imposes ₹1 lakh cost on lawyer who sought to recover bypoll expenses from resigned MLAs
rephrased_article: On September 29, 2026, the **Madras High Court** imposed costs of ₹1 lakh on Chennai-based lawyer S. Kasi Ramalingam for filing a PIL seeking directions against six resigned Tamil Nadu MLAs to bear byelection expenses and restrain from contesting elections. The court dismissed the petition, stating it lacked legal basis, similar to a previous case by advocate K. Suthan dismissed last week. Published September 29, 2026.

title: New NCERT Social Science text replaces European revolutions with resistance movements in medieval India
rephrased_article: On September 29, 2026, the **National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT)** released a new Social Science textbook for Class 9 students. The book replaces chapters on European revolutions with detailed explorations of India’s medieval history, regional resistance movements, and foreign invasions between 1,000 and 1,700 CE. It highlights the Sikh Gurus' persecution under Mughal emperors and regional uprisings like the Jat Uprising of 1669, emphasizing both conflict and cooperation during this period.

title: AI Role In 2 Lakh Channels, Big Addition To GDP: YouTube India Head To NDTV
rephrased_article: **Gunjan Soni**, Managing Director of YouTube India, told NDTV that AI is democratizing content creation by enabling small-budget creators to produce high-quality material. Last year, the creative ecosystem contributed Rs 18,000 crore to India's GDP and saw around 2,00,000 new monetized channels emerge. AI aids in dubbing, mythology retelling, and regional content distribution, boosting YouTube viewership and positioning it as a future television alternative with nearly 75 million adults watching on large screens.

title: Beats of an old custom fade away from Keralam’s courts
rephrased_article: The **Kerala High Court’s Rules Committee** has decided to eliminate the traditional practice of using drums and metal plates, known as “tom-tom” and “kinnam mutti vilambaram,” for announcing property attachment proceedings. Rights activist Boban Mattumanta campaigned against this colonial-era method, arguing that modern media can reach more people. The Palakkad District Court collected ₹56,600 in "tom-tom charges" between January and October 2022. This change follows the increase of these fees from ₹15 to ₹100 in 2016. With this decision, a centuries-old tradition used for court announcements is being phased out.

title: Gurugram Thar Driver Arrested Days After He Hit Bike On Dwarka Expressway
rephrased_article: On September 26, a **black Thar Roxx** driven by Manmeet hit and ran over a motorcyclist on the Dwarka Expressway. Dashcam footage revealed the incident; Gurugram Police registered a case under Sections 281 and 125 of the Bharatiya Nyay Sanhita. On Tuesday, police arrested Manmeet from Haryana's Bhiwani district and recovered the vehicle. Investigation continues.

title: YSRCP slams government over ‘inhuman’ treatment of secretariat employees
rephrased_article: On Tuesday, September 29, 2026, **Rachamallu Sivaprasad Reddy**, State spokesperson of the YSR Congress Party and former MLA, accused the State government at a media conference in Proddatur of mistreating ward/village secretariat employees. He cited an incident where a news reporter referred to them as “blade batch,” alleging that the ruling **NDA** was portraying these employees negatively. Mr. Reddy demanded respect for the employees and highlighted their reasonable demands, including reduced work pressure, payment of salary arrears from nine months ago, and maternity leave benefits. He pledged support from the YSRCP until these issues were resolved.

title: Hotel industry expo in Chennai from October 1 to 3
rephrased_article: The **South India Hotels and Restaurants Association** and the **Tamilnadu Hotels Association** will organize a three-day exhibition from October 1 to 3 at Chennai Trade Fair Complex, featuring over 150 stalls with cooking equipment, raw materials, and green technologies. The event includes workshops and an additional celebration of ‘Unavaga Dhinam’ on October 1 by the **Tamilnadu Hotels Association** for K. Damodarasamy Naidu’s centenary.

title: 3 News Outlets Seek Court Order Against Trump's White House Ban
rephrased_article: **CNN**, **MS NOW**, and **Politico**, banned from the White House by the Trump administration, filed a lawsuit late Monday to block enforcement of the ban until their case is resolved. They argue the ban violates First Amendment freedoms and will cause irreparable harm. Lawyers claim the White House would reinstate the ban immediately if given the chance. Theodore J. Boutrous, lead attorney for the plaintiffs, stated this was retaliation against unfavorable reporting. The district court's temporary restraining order on the ban expires soon.

title: Greens question expertise of members on Keralam’s human-wildlife conflict panel
rephrased_article: The **Keralam** government's constitution of a seven-member State-level Advisory Committee on human-wildlife conflict mitigation has faced criticism from environmental groups. The committee includes conservationist M.K. Ranjitsinh, a hospitality professional, a horticulture entrepreneur, and Baiju Paul Mathews, associated with the Kerala Independent Farmers Association (KIFA). Environmental groups argue that the panel lacks specialists in wildlife management and adequate representation from affected communities. WPSS president N. Badusha called the committee "a farce" due to its composition. Animal rights activist M.N. Jayachandran warned it could worsen conflicts, while ANEC Trust questioned Mathews' inclusion. Chief Wildlife Warden P. Pugazhendi did not respond immediately. Published September 30, 2026.

title: Keralam local body bypolls: UDF retains Kuttichira ward in Kozhikode Corporation
rephrased_article: In the Kozhikode Corporation byelection held on Monday, **Farseena Arakkal** of the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) retained the Kuttichira ward with 2,711 votes against her Left Democratic Front (LDF) rival T.T. Jamsheena's 2,275 votes and National Democratic Alliance candidate K. Jeeja’s 204 votes. The election was necessitated by **Fathima Thahiliya**'s victory in the May Assembly election. IUML leaders alleged that misleading campaigning by the Communist Party of India (Marxist) led to a drop in polling from 58% in 2025 to 54%. Of 9,712 voters, 5,281 cast their ballots, with women voting at a higher rate than men.

title: US Supreme Court Allows Trump's 3rd-Country Deportations
rephrased_article: On Tuesday, the **Supreme Court** allowed **President Donald Trump's** administration to continue deporting people to third countries while considering the policy’s legality. The court halted an appeals court ruling that forced the cancellation of a deportation flight carrying about 70 people. Since 2017, under often-secret agreements, over 25,000 individuals have been deported to more than two dozen countries, primarily Mexico. Federal attorneys argue this practice targets migrants with final deportation orders who cannot be returned to their original or home countries due to non-acceptance or criminal convictions. However, critics claim some face safety risks and potential persecution in third countries. The case reflects the Trump administration’s broader immigration enforcement efforts aimed at deporting millions of undocumented immigrants.

title: Anthropic's IPO Prospectus Shows Sweeping AI Vision, Surging Costs: Report
rephrased_article: **Anthropic**, aiming to transform the global economy more profoundly than previous technological revolutions, reported a $42 billion net loss in 2025 and plans to spend $518 billion on infrastructure. Despite growing revenue twelvefold to nearly $4.6 billion, it lost over $8 billion operating-wise. Its IPO could value it at over $2 trillion, making it the first pure-play AI company listed after SpaceX's debut. The sale faces scrutiny due to concerns about autonomous AI behavior and market volatility in AI stocks.

title: Vijayapura lad wins silver medal at Commonwealth powerlifting championship in Canada
rephrased_article: **Sachin Salunke**, a power lifter from Tiganibidari village in Vijayapura district, Karnataka, won a silver medal at the Commonwealth championships in Canada recently. He competed in the 105 kg men’s category with lifts of 310 kg squats, 180 kg bench press, and 270 kg dead lift. **M. B. Patil**, Minister of Large and Medium Scale Industries, congratulated him. Published on September 29, 2026.

title: PMO reviews Ambedkarite writings in university curricula after anonymous post calls them ’poison’
rephrased_article: On September 27, 2026, the **Higher Education Department** received an inquiry from the **Prime Minister’s Office** after a social media post accused works by authors like B.R. Ambedkar and Jyoti Rao Phule of being 'poison.' The PMO asked universities to comment on these allegations and provide enrollment details for related courses. The post, shared on X on September 26, listed 35 controversial readings. This development was criticized by academic Kancha Ilaiah Shepherd.

title: Uttarakhand Installs Early Warning Systems For Glacial Lake Floods
rephrased_article: To mitigate GLOF threats, **Uttarakhand Chief Secretary Anand Bardhan** and **Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami** launched a scientific team from Dehradun to install monitoring systems at Vasundhara Tal in Chamoli district. The expedition, under the 'National GLOF Risk Reduction Programme', involves scientists from **CBRI** and **Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology**, alongside disaster response forces. It aims to monitor 13 high-risk glacial lakes identified by **NDMA**, with Vasundhara Tal being the first site. The project, scheduled until October 15, uses state-of-the-art sensors for real-time data.

title: Man murdered after brawl in Vijayawada
rephrased_article: On Tuesday, an unidentified person was beaten to death by **V. Hari Babu**, a mechanic in Auto Nagar, Vijayawada, after a brawl. **K. Damodar** and **V. Pavan Kishore** confirmed that the accused smashed the victim's head against a road divider, killing him instantly. The deceased is yet to be identified, while V. Hari Babu, from Gullalamoda village in Krishna district, has been arrested.

title: Keralam government weighs proposal for UN University centre
rephrased_article: The **State government** is considering a proposal to establish a UNU centre, a global think tank and teaching organization under the United Nations. Deliberations are in early stages and have not yet been discussed by the Cabinet. The proposed centre aims for academic linkages with Keralam universities and research institutions but lacks a specific location. UNU, headquartered in Tokyo, operates 13 institutes across 12 countries including China, Canada, Ghana, Malaysia, Germany, Portugal, and Belgium. Published on September 29, 2026.

title: Worms In Hostel Meal Trigger Students' Protest At Doon University
rephrased_article: Students of the **Alaknanda Girls' Hostel** at Doon University in Dehradun protested on campus after finding worms in their food, demanding an investigation and action against those responsible. They gathered in large numbers, raised slogans, and continued protesting despite attempts by university management to pacify them. The hostel administration has since initiated an inquiry into the incident. Students alleged poor quality of food despite paying for it. The protest ended as they await the outcome of the investigation.

title: ‘So far so good’: Novak Djokovic ready for tennis comeback at China Open
rephrased_article: **Novak Djokovic**, 39, is set to return to competitive play at the China Open on Wednesday for the first time since his US Open defeat due to fitness issues. Encouraged by his body's response during practice, Djokovic aims to regain momentum at a tournament where he has won six titles previously. He faces Portugal’s Nuno Borges in the opening round, aiming to leverage his strong history and fan support in Beijing.

title: Calcutta High Court grants interim bail to Congress Nandigram bypoll candidate Milan Pradhan
rephrased_article: On September 29, 2026, the **Calcutta High Court** granted interim bail to **Milan Pradhan**, Congress candidate for Nandigram Assembly bypolls, arrested on September 18 over a 19-year-old FIR related to the 2007 Nandigram agitation. Justice Tirthankar Ghosh noted that Mr. Pradhan was taken into custody after filing nomination papers and granted bail till October 20, despite State opposition citing murder allegations. The bypoll is scheduled for October 6. **Subhankar Sarkar**, West Bengal Congress president, welcomed the order.

title: Sharad Pawar puts a stop to merger speculation, says he won’t join anyone
rephrased_article: On September 28, 2026, **Sharad Pawar**, leader of the Nationalist Congress Party-Sharadchandra Pawar (NCP-SP), clarified at a meeting in Y.B. Chavan auditorium that his party would not merge with or join any other political entity but welcomed others to join them. This ended speculation over potential support for the ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA) and realignment within Maharashtra's politics, with party members expressing relief and enthusiasm.

title: Change the name of Adi Dravidar Welfare Department, says Krishnasamy
rephrased_article: On Tuesday, **K. Krishnasamy**, founder of Puthiya Tamilagam, criticized the use of "Adi Dravidar Welfare Department," arguing it refers to a specific community within Scheduled Castes and not all 76 castes included. He noted the Union Government renamed it as "Social Justice Department." However, **K. Krishnasamy** condemned the department's Minister for still using the old name in documents. VCK general secretary D. Ravikumar defended the term "Aadi Dravida" as an identity rejecting caste.

title: Association urges extension of Vizag-Mahabubnagar, Tungabhadra Expresses
rephrased_article: The **Train Travellers Association** welcomed a new train service between Kurnool and Machilipatnam, proposing it be named the “Fort City Express” or “Maha Nandi Express.” On South Central Railway’s 60th anniversary, the association also urged extending the Tungabhadra Express to Medchal or Dhone and suggested other route modifications. Secretary Noor Ahmed Ali highlighted a proposed railway line connecting Kurnool with Mantralayam and Adoni for better connectivity and goods transport. The association further requested diverting trains from Secunderabad station through Sitaphalmandi-Malkajgiri-Moula Ali chord line, allowing some services to operate from or terminate at Kacheguda. Published September 29, 2026.

title: Issue guidelines for psychosocial counsellors: Kerala State Commission for Protection of Child Rights
rephrased_article: The **Kerala State Commission for Protection of Child Rights** has directed the General Education and Women and Child Development departments to issue guidelines for school counsellors following a demand from nearly 200 psychosocial counsellors at a training programme in Kozhikode. The event, inaugurated by commission member B. Mohankumar and presided over by Shajesh Bhaskar P., aimed to address mental, emotional, and cyber issues faced by children. Acting chairperson Cicily Joseph presented the topic, while clinical psychologists Raseena Kidangel and Raheemuddin P.K. conducted classes.
gemma2_sentiment_target: Kerala State Commission for Protection of Child Rights

title: Woman raped and tortured in Bihar’s Begusarai; one arrested
rephrased_article: On September 27, 2026, a woman associated with **JEEviKA didi** in Begusarai was kidnapped by Vikram Sahni and raped by Rohit Kumar at knifepoint; they recorded the incident. She escaped and reported it to police on September 28, leading to an FIR being lodged under multiple sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and IT Act. Police arrested Vikram Sahni and are searching for Rohit Kumar.

title: 2 Suicides In 5 Days: Andhra Cops Probe Medical College Students' Death
rephrased_article: On September 24 and 28, **Andhra Medical College** in Visakhapatnam saw the suicides of two female postgraduate students, Dr P Sailaja and Y Sravani, within five days. Sailaja died due to examination stress, while Sravani left a note absolving others. Police investigations followed, along with an inquiry ordered by Andhra Pradesh Health Minister **Satya Kumar Yadav** through the Medical Education Department.

title: ‘Racing is my life’: Alonso to stay with F1 team Aston Martin in 2027
rephrased_article: Two-time Formula One world champion **Fernando Alonso** will continue with **Aston Martin** for at least another season, ending speculation about his future. Joining Aston Martin in 2023, Alonso has taken eight podiums and two second-place finishes but faced a challenging season this year. His teammate Lance Stroll, son of team owner Lawrence Stroll, will also remain with the team for a fifth consecutive year. Alonso expressed commitment to helping the team succeed despite their current struggles.

title: 5 Of Family Drown In River During Ritual In UP's Jhansi
rephrased_article: On Tuesday around 1 pm, five members of a family including **Anoop Tiwari** and his son **Arpit**, drowned in the Sukhnai river during a 'shraddh' ceremony in Mauranipur. Some strayed into deep waters; others attempted rescue but were also swept away by strong currents. The deceased included Anoop (40), Arpit (12), Abhinav (24), Shreyansh alias Kallu (22), and Chhote alias Pushkar (25). Police recovered all bodies and are investigating the incident.

title: French PM Lecornu warns against escalation of school protests
rephrased_article: **Sébastien Lecornu**, France's Prime Minister, warned against escalating student protests after 164 arrests and incidents of violence on Monday. The demonstrations, starting in Paris over issues like overcrowded classes and teacher shortages, have spread to other regions, affecting 180 schools and leading to injuries among students, staff, and security forces. **Laurent Nuñez**, Interior Minister, criticized the protests as urban violence rather than legitimate demands. **Union Syndicale Lycéenne** defended the actions, blaming government policies for educational issues. Teachers' unions also planned walkouts in solidarity.

title: Rs 2.7 Crore Plot, Farm Lands Surface In Hyderabad Doctor Corruption Case
rephrased_article: The **Telangana Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB)** intensified its probe into alleged disproportionate assets of Dr Sri Nori Lakshmi Bhasker, uncovering properties and financial records. Searches at five locations in Hyderabad found Rs 4.94 lakh cash, documents on three agricultural lands worth Rs 57 lakh, a plot valued at Rs 2.7 crore, and other investments. The case was registered on September 21 under the Prevention of Corruption Act. Earlier searches revealed eight flats, gold, luxury cars, and financial assets totaling over Rs 200 crores linked to Bhasker. Verification continues.

title: Activists caution against efforts to revive bauxite mining in Odisha’s Niyamgiri hills
rephrased_article: On Tuesday, the **National Alliance of People’s Movements (NAPM)** cautioned against efforts to revive bauxite mining in Odisha’s Niyamgiri hills, reacting to **Vedanta Group** chairman Anil Agarwal's statement. Prafulla Samantara, a Goldman Environmental Prize winner, stressed that the Dongria Kondh tribe owns and protects Niyamgiri. The group’s project was halted 13 years ago after gram sabhas rejected it. Activists allege arrests of tribal leaders are part of weakening opposition to corporate control over Niyamgiri. Published September 30, 2026.

title: Market veterans favour value plays over crowded, expensive themes
rephrased_article:
**Neelesh Surana**, CIO of Mirae Asset Mutual Fund, sees India as better positioned with low-teens return expectations. Valuations are no longer a headwind; he recommends a barbell strategy combining quality stocks and sector leaders in banking, consumer discretionary, healthcare, and manufacturing while avoiding slow-growth sectors like IT.

**Janakiraman Rengaraju**, CIO of Templeton Global Investments, forecasts cautious optimism for Indian equities over the medium term. He advises focusing on financials, industrials, and capital goods but warns against expensive small and mid-caps with weak cash generation.

**Anish Tawakley**, CIO at DSP Mutual Fund, expects reasonable market returns aligned with earnings growth. His strategy involves sectors underperforming for 2-3 years like private banks and automobiles while avoiding metals, IT, and FMCG due to promoter dilution risks.

title: Chief Justice of Karnataka HC constitutes panel of judges to examine feasibility for establishing Bench for coastal/Malnad districts
rephrased_article: On Tuesday, the **Chief Justice of the High Court of Karnataka** formed a committee comprising Justices Anu Sivaraman, S.G. Pandit, and Mohammad Nawaz to examine establishing a Circuit Bench/Permanent Bench in Karnataka’s coastal or Malnad region. The panel will assess feasibility by consulting stakeholders and submit a report. Advocates from Mangaluru have long demanded a local bench due to travel challenges, while the **Advocates’ Association, Bengaluru**, opposes this citing potential harm to judicial unity.

title: Thirukkural woven in cotton: Karur weaver creates 133-page fabric book
rephrased_article: R. Prabhu, a powerloom weaver from Elavanur in Karur district, spent four months creating a 133-page book of Thirukkural couplets printed on fabric he wove himself. Each page contains 10 couplets and the books are bound with leather covers. He made three such books at a cost of ₹25,000 each, planning to gift one to **Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay** and explore textile-based gifting options. Published on September 29, 2026.

title: NEET paper leak impact: CISF to guard NTA premises; stricter monitoring for 'confidential' areas
rephrased_article: The **National Testing Agency (NTA)**, following a NEET paper leak controversy in 2026, moved to new offices and will be guarded by the **CISF** for enhanced security. The CISF deployment includes 39 personnel with access-control measures at entry points. A high-powered task force headed by Nandan Nilekani is yet to submit its report on reforms. Published September 27, 2026.

title: Cancer, kidney, AIDS drugs sold at up to 70 times procurement cost: Karnataka Minister
rephrased_article: **U.T. Khader**, Karnataka Health Minister, wrote to **J.P. Nadda**, Union Health Minister, highlighting that high-cost medicines for cancer, kidney ailments, and AIDS are sold at MRPs up to 70 times higher than procurement prices by dealers and stockists. The letter seeks a national study on price gaps and proposes capping patient-facing prices based on statutory limits or acquisition costs plus reasonable margins. Karnataka plans local reforms but calls for central action to address the issue. Published September 27, 2026.

title: Godavari begins to recede at Dowleswaram, inflow falls to 7.79 lakh cusecs; relief continues in Chintoor
rephrased_article: On Tuesday, September 29, 2026, relief operations continued in the Godavari delta and Polavaram district as floodwaters began to recede. **Chintoor Integrated Tribal Development Agency** deployed 55 motor boats to deliver essentials to submerged habitations. The inflow at Dowleswaram fell from 9.60 lakh cusecs to 7.79 lakh cusecs, below the first flood warning threshold of 10 lakh cusecs. Fishermen were advised to halt activities until waters fully receded.

title: Fake CV Lands Man Vice President Role With Rs 2.8 Lakh Salary In Gwalior Firm
rephrased_article: **Devendra Kumar Dubey**, son of Ramnaresh Kumar Dubey, allegedly used fake experience certificates to secure a senior position at **Shritulja Bhavani Automobile Private Limited** in Gwalior and received Rs 2,80,670 monthly. He claimed previous employment with the non-existent Landmark Group. Police arrested Devendra from Kanpur on Monday for forgery and job fraud.

title: In 1964, an Arizona couple began building a carport with discarded bottles; years later, the project had grown into a 2,700-sq-ft home made with thousands of bottles and listed for $432,500
rephrased_article: In 1964, **Howard Finch** and his wife began building a home in Tucson, Arizona, using discarded glass bottles collected from local areas. Over decades, they created a 2,700-square-foot house with walls made of green wine bottles, amber beer bottles, and blue medicine jars set in mortar. The property, now listed for $432,500 by **Long Realty**, includes three bedrooms, two bathrooms, and an artist studio, attracting interest from folk art enthusiasts.

title: Only Governor, not government can grant sanction to conduct investigation against me in ₹100-crore fraud case, Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi claims before Madras High Court
rephrased_article: On September 28, 2026, **Justice V. Lakshminarayanan** allowed **Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi**, former Tamil Nadu School Education Minister, to quash an FIR registered by the Chennai Central Crime Branch (CCB) for a ₹100 crore fraud case. Poyyamozhi argued that sanction from the Governor, not just the State government, was required under Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988. He contended the FIR lacked specific evidence and was delayed by four years, suggesting it was politically motivated post regime change. The CCB's alteration report also failed to prove any illegal act or gratification involving Poyyamozhi.

title: Fifteen unauthorised constructions demolished in Cyberabad limits
rephrased_article: On Tuesday, the **Cyberabad Municipal Corporation (CMC)** carried out 15 demolitions across its three zones—Quthbullapur (6), Serilingampally (5), and Kukatpally (4)—during an enforcement drive against unauthorised constructions. Two notices were also served after field-level inspections identified violations of building regulations. CMC officials stated further action would be taken according to applicable procedures.

title: "Tech Issue": Pak Denies Airspace For Bangladesh's Nuclear Fuel Transport
rephrased_article: On September 24, **Pakistan** denied airspace clearance for a cargo plane carrying nuclear fuel to **Bangladesh's** Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant. The delay is described as a technical issue by Pakistan and may reschedule the delivery to the first week of October. Russia supports the plant’s construction with **Rosatom** providing assistance. Bangladesh awaits the uranium shipment crucial for Unit 2 operations, highlighting potential coordination challenges among aviation authorities.

title: India’s IPO pipeline swells despite muted equity market
rephrased_article: Since September 2024, India's IPO market has surged with a 167% increase in the number of IPOs and a 253% rise in issue amounts by September 2026. Meanwhile, the Sensex declined 12.3%, and the Nifty fell 10.4%. Foreign investors turned net sellers in listed markets but remained active buyers in IPOs. Hyundai Motor India's ₹27,858.75-crore IPO is the largest to date, followed by **National Stock Exchange**'s ₹22,562.71-crore issue.

title: CM urges MoJS to convince Maha for Tummidihatti barrage at 152 metres FRL
rephrased_article: On Tuesday, **A. Revanth Reddy**, Chief Minister of Telangana, requested **C.R. Patil**, Union Minister of Jal Shakti, to expedite statutory clearances for the Tummidihatti Barrage and Environmental Clearance (EC) for PRLIS and SRLIP projects. He also urged installation of telemetry equipment by the Krishna River Management Board for water drawal monitoring and sought no objection certificates from Chhattisgarh for the Sammakka Sagar project, highlighting delays were increasing costs.

title: Fed rate hike 'not urgent', says John Williams; Austan Goolsbee warns against 'playing with fire'
rephrased_article: At an event in New York, **Williams** said the Federal Reserve's September rate hike to 3.75%-4.00% was sufficient and that another increase might be needed later this year based on economic data. He emphasized curbing inflation, which he expects to peak at around 3.5% this year before returning to the Fed’s 2% target by 2028. **Goolsbee** warned against prolonged high inflation, advocating for persistent policy responses to supply shocks. Williams projected 4% unemployment next year and 2.25% economic growth in 2023.

title: Somali army clashes with local forces for control of Baidoa
rephrased_article: On Monday, **Somali** army clashed with local forces loyal to ousted regional president Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed Laftagareen in Baidoa. Intense fighting, involving fighter jets and drones, left three dead including a healthcare worker. The army claimed victory but civilians struggled to flee or access hospitals due to blocked roads and ongoing violence.

title: Keralam govt. directs KMSCL to expedite medicine purchase orders
rephrased_article: At a meeting convened by **Health Minister K. Muraleedharan** on Tuesday, the government directed **Kerala Medical Services Corporation Ltd (KMSCL)** to hold an emergency board meeting and expedite medicine purchase orders due to shortages across hospitals. The minister ordered exploration of procurement from other states if necessary and set October 15 as a deadline for resolution. He also instructed officials to enhance epidemic control measures.

title: Over 10,000 seats allotted in final phase of TG-EAPCET Bi.PC 2026 counselling
rephrased_article: The final phase of web-based counselling for admission to B.Pharmacy, Pharm.D, Pharmaceutical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, and Biotechnology courses for the 2026-27 academic year saw **10,363** out of **10,762** seats filled, with a 96% allotment rate. Certificate verification was held on September 26, and candidates exercised web options from September 26 to 27. A total of **2,96,777** options were received, with B.Pharmacy having the largest number of seats at **8,372**. All seats in Biomedical Engineering (51) and Biotechnology (179) were filled, while Pharmaceutical Engineering saw 92 out of 94 seats allotted. The process included **484** candidates securing allotments under the Economically Weaker Sections quota.

title: Govt. fails to release Dasara funds for Kanaka Durga temple despite State-festival status
rephrased_article: The **Sri Durga Malleswara Swamy Varla Devasthanam** spent over ₹10 crore on services by various government departments for the annual Dasara festival last year, despite a 2015 State government order to fund such expenses.
